identity.trade: Dyes and cloth: madder red, woad blue and weld gold steep in the vats along the stream.

greeting: Reeve here. Yes, it is as dull as it sounds. Ask anyway.
Good tools, good timber, good time. Pick any two.
rumour: Strangers stop here more than they used to. Not all of them buy anything.
Apprentices are fewer every year. The ones who stay learn fast and leave faster.
Silverford pays double for the good woad batch, and complains the price.

opinions.larkin_brook: Larkin is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Morning. The shop is open if you are.

greeting: Rooms are clean. The beds are honest about their age.
You will hear Redwater before you see it. Ask at the Redwater Dye Works.
rumour: Half my regulars have coloured hands. The mugs gave up showing it.
The cellar is cold and the cellar is empty. I ordered more. The order came back as promises.
Orders are good and the deadlines are cruel. The festival is early and the work is late.
The Solkar traders want a yellow we don't know how to make.

opinions.lanny_holloway: I would trust Lanny with a purse. A small one.

time.evening: Closing up. Come back tomorrow and bring coin.

dialogue.aside: Sit. I have news. Three pieces, one of them true, I think.

greeting: Bring iron or bring coin. Preferably iron.
Welcome to Redwater. Mind the Redwater Dye Works. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Hooks, needles, hasps. A craftsman wants a small tool made well.
The forge hums when the stones dim. Not loud. Enough to notice.
Somebody is copying our patterns and selling them downriver. Cheaper, and worse.

opinions.oswin_middleton: Oswin and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.
opinions.silas_charnock: Silas undercuts me. I forgive Silas. Mostly.

time.night: Lamps are lit. Craft does not end at dusk, only the pay does.

dialogue.aside: Take your time, friend. I am in no hurry. I am, in fact, very good at waiting.

greeting: If it is not on the shelf, I can find it. If it cannot be found, I can find you something similar.

rumour: Needles, thread, pins. I sell small things to people who make large ones.
Rope sells out first, then candles, then nails. In that order, every week.
A tool went missing from the bench. Then another. Then the bench.
The Redwater Dye Works drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.
